Count the permutations in each case by treating each required substring as a single block.

**p₁:** AB, CD and EF each become one block. That leaves 26 − 6 = 20 other letters plus 3 blocks, so 23 objects, which can be arranged in 23! ways. So p₁ = 23!/26!.

**p₂:** ABC and DEF each become one block. That leaves 26 − 6 = 20 other letters plus 2 blocks, so 22 objects, which can be arranged in 22! ways. So p₂ = 22!/26!.

**Ratio:** p₁/p₂ = 23!/22! = 23.

ANSWER: 23
